_tools_list.name: query_fsm_postgres
_tools_list.description:
Execute queries against FortiSIEM PostgreSQL database.

# Guidance for Postgres Selection/Handoff:

Use PostgreSQL Agent under the following circumstances:
        1. User is explicitly asking to use Postgres.
        2. User is asking about Incidents triggered by FortiSIEM:
            
              Example questions:
                - Tell me what you know about a specific incident
                - Get Incidents involving a specific host or a device or an user 
                - Get Incidents involving host HOST-203.0.113.1
                - Get Incidents involving user admin
                - Get latest 10 high severity Incidents
                - Get most frequent 10 Incidents      
        3. User is asking questions about Organizations, Hosts, devices, users and their properties
                Example questions:
                   - What are the Organizations in my CMDB
                   - How many devices in my CMDB Group by Organization.
                   - Categorize CMDB devices by discovery method
                   - List all network interfaces of a device or host
                   - Show me applications installed on a device
                   - Show me running processes on a device 
                   - How many FortiSIEM administrator users in CMDB 
                   - Show me all CMDB devices with Critical event collection status
                   - Show me all CMDB devices with Critical monitoring status 

        4.  User is asking questions about FortiSIEM Health and Environment:  
              
              Example Qquestions:
               - Tell me about my FortiSIEM environmentt
               - How is the current overall health of the various FortiSIEM nodes?


        5. User is asking about User Identity and Location Records
            


This tool should be used together with the "query_fsm_postgres_prompts" prompt,
which provides the necessary guidance for SQL generation for PostgreSQL database.

_tools_list.name: query_fsm_clickhouse
_tools_list.description:
Execute queries against FortiSIEM Clickhouse database.

# Guidance for ClickHouse Selection/Handoff:

Use ClickHouse Agent under the following circumstances::
        1. User is explicitly asking to use ClickHouse.
        2. User is asking questions about Logs or Events:
            
            Example questions:
                - Which top 10 devices are sending the most amount of events in last 1 hour? 
                - Get Reporting Devices that sent logs yesterday but not did not send any today
                - Are there any logs or events related to a specific vulnerability e.g. CVE-2023-48795?
                - Are there any logs or events related to a specific IP or a host name or a user?
                - Analyze logs to see which vulnerabilities (CVEs) are present in my environment  
        3. User is asking about events generated by devices
            Example questions:
                - Get top 10 event types for devices in Firewall group for last 1 hour. 
   
 

This tool should be used together with the "query_fsm_clickhouse_prompts" prompt,
which provides the necessary guidance for SQL generation for Clickhouse database.

_tools_list.name: get_incidents_by_entity
_tools_list.description:
Retrieve Active Incidents for the last N hours or days current time. If a specific entity
(e.g. IP address, hostname, or user) is provided, then only Incidents related to that entity
will be retrieved.
    - Input is a time period (e.g. 2 hours or 1 day) and optionally one entity. The entity
    should be exactly one of "ip, hostname, or username" can be provided. The match is
    case-insensitive.
    - Returns incident ID, incident title, severity, status, first and last seen times
    for matching each incident.

Use this as the starting point for any incident investigation for an entity.
Example:
    - Get all the incident on host 'abc.com' for the past 24 hours, the params would be like:
        {
            "time_value": 24,
            "time_unit": "hours",
            "hostname": "abc.com"
        }

EntityIncidentQuery.description:
Filter parameters for querying incidents over a time window.
Exactly one of ip, hostname, or username must be provided.

time_value.description: Number of time units to look back (e.g. 24)
time_value.title: Time Value

_tools_list.name: get_incident_by_id
_tools_list.description:
Retrieve detail information for a specific incident ID.
    - Input is one incident id. Exactly one incident id can be provided.
    - Returns the following information for the give incident id:
        incident title, severity, status, resolution, first and last seen times, rule name,
        incident source, incident target, incident details, tags, tactics, technique,
        category, subcategory.

Use this as the starting point for any incident investigation for an incident id.
Example:
    - Get all the incident information for incident 111, the params would be like:
        {
            "incident_id": 111
        }

IncidentId.description: A non-empty list of incident ID to act on.
IncidentId.title: IncidentId

_tools_list.name: get_related_incidents_by_id
_tools_list.description:
Retrieve the active incidents related to a specific incident ID. An incident is related to
another incident if they have a common IP or host name in incident source or target.
This API can be used to discovered an attack chain involving multiple hosts.
    - Input is one incident id. Exactly one incident id can be provided.
    - Returns details for a maximum of 100 related incidents:
        Incident Id, Title, Status, Last Occurred

Example:
    - Get all the related incident information for incident 111, the params would be like:
        {
            "incident_id": 111
        }

IncidentId.description: A non-empty list of incident ID to act on.
IncidentId.title: IncidentId

_tools_list.name: get_trigger_events_by_incident_id
_tools_list.description:
Retrieve details of events that triggered a specific incident ID.
    - Input is one incident id. Exactly one incident id can be provided.
    - Returns a maximum of 10 triggering event details:
        receive time, event id, event type, source IP, source name, destination IP,
        destination name, user, target user and raw message.

Example:
    - Get all the events that triggered incident 111, the params would be like:
        {
            "incident_id": 111
        }

IncidentId.description: A non-empty list of incident ID to act on.

                # Questions regarding Organizations or Customers
                FortiSIEM Organizations (also known as Customers) - each entity like device, event, incident belong to an Organization. There is 1 Organization called Super
                   ## Relevant Tables:
                       ph_sys_domain: contains all Organizations; important columns are 
                                 - domain_id: id of the Organization: 1: Super; others may be defined by user; ignore 0 and 2; user defined organizations have value other than 0,1,2
                                 - name: name of the Organization

                       ## Examples:
                        Question - What are the Organizations in CMDB?
                        SELECT domain_id AS "Org Id", name "Org Name" from ph_sys_domain where domain_id NOT IN (0,2);

                        Question - What are the User defined Organizations in CMDB?
                        SELECT domain_id AS "Org Id", name AS "Org Name" from ph_sys_domain where domain_id NOT IN (0,1,2);

                # Questions related to a device or a host 
                
                    ## Relevant Tables:
                        ph_device : contains basic information about a device; important columns are 
                                        - name: device or host name. When checking for device name match, it is better to use ILIKE SQL operator rather than '='
                                        - access_ip: the IP address using which the device was discovered. All other IP are stored in ph_device_intf table
                                        - id: primary key - used to join with other tables
					- device_type_id - id of the device type in the ph_device_type table. Use this to join with the ph_device_type

                            to_timestamp(inc.last_seen_time/1000), 
                            CASE inc.incident_reso
                                WHEN 2 THEN 'True Positive'
                                WHEN 3 THEN 'False Positive'
                                ELSE 'Unknown'
                                END AS Resolution,
                                confidence

                        WHERE inc.last_seen_time > (EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM date_trunc('day', now())) * 1000) AND inc.comments ilike '%Resolution set by Machine Learning%'

                    Question - Which IP has triggered more than 1 distinct tactics today? Show IPs and the tactics in a comma separated list.
                        -- Note - To resolve this check all 3 attributes: src_ip_addr, dest_ip_addr, host_ip_addr. First form a union, then split tactics by comma and then count distinct

                        WITH Host_Tactics AS (
    					SELECT inc.src_ip_addr AS ip, d.name AS Org, inc.tactics AS tactics, COUNT(*) AS cnt
    					FROM ph_incident inc JOIN ph_sys_domain d ON d.domain_id = inc.cust_org_id 
    					WHERE inc.src_ip_addr IS NOT NULL AND inc.tactics IS NOT NULL AND inc.last_seen_time > (EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM date_trunc('day', now())) * 1000)
    					GROUP BY inc.src_ip_addr, d.name, inc.tactics

    					UNION ALL

    					SELECT inc.dest_ip_addr AS ip, d.name AS Org, inc.tactics AS tactics, COUNT(*) AS cnt
    					FROM ph_incident inc JOIN ph_sys_domain d ON d.domain_id = inc.cust_org_id 
    					WHERE inc.dest_ip_addr IS NOT NULL AND inc.tactics IS NOT NULL AND inc.last_seen_time > (EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM date_trunc('day', now())) * 1000)
    					GROUP BY inc.dest_ip_addr, d.name, inc.tactics

    					UNION ALL

    					SELECT inc.host_ip_addr AS ip, d.name AS Org, inc.tactics AS tactics, COUNT(*) AS cnt
    					FROM ph_incident inc JOIN ph_sys_domain d ON d.domain_id = inc.cust_org_id 
    					WHERE inc.host_ip_addr IS NOT NULL AND inc.tactics IS NOT NULL AND inc.last_seen_time > (EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM date_trunc('day', now())) * 1000)
    					GROUP BY inc.host_ip_addr, d.name, inc.tactics
				  ),
				  Host_Tactics_Exploded AS (
    					SELECT ip, Org, trim(tactic) AS tactic
    					FROM Host_Tactics, unnest(string_to_array(tactics, ',')) AS t(tactic)
				  )

				  SELECT ip, Org, COUNT(DISTINCT tactic) AS tactic_count, STRING_AGG(DISTINCT tactic, ', ' ORDER BY tactic) AS tactics_list
				  FROM Host_Tactics_Exploded
				  GROUP BY ip, Org
				  HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT tactic) > 1
				  ORDER BY tactic_count DESC;

                 Question - Tell me the Active/Open Incidents related to a given incident id. Provide Incident Id, Title, Status, Last Occurred

            WITH related_inc AS (
